questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Meaning of International Business' refers to.
questions.a: International business refers to business transactions that take place across national boundaries and include trade in goods and services, movement of capital, technology, and personnel between countries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Meaning of International Business'.
questions.a: International business extends business activity beyond national borders and involves cross-border exchange of goods, services, capital, and knowledge.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Meaning of International Business'.
questions.a: What is international business?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Reasons for International Business' refers to.
questions.a: International business arises because countries differ in their resources, technology, labour, and demand, and because no single country can produce all goods efficiently or meet all its needs alone.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Reasons for International Business'.
questions.a: Nations engage in international business to obtain goods they cannot produce, benefit from cost advantages, achieve economies of scale, and reduce dependence on a single market.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Reasons for International Business'.
questions.a: Why do countries engage in international business?

concepts.title: Modes of Entry into International Business

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Modes of Entry into International Business' refers to.
questions.a: Modes of entry into international business are the different ways a firm can enter foreign markets, including export and import, licensing and franchising, joint ventures, and wholly owned subsidiaries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Modes of Entry into International Business'.
questions.a: A firm chooses its entry mode based on the level of control, investment, risk, and involvement it wants in a foreign market, ranging from simple export to full ownership.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Modes of Entry into International Business'.
questions.a: What are the modes of entry into international business?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Export and Import Trade' refers to.
questions.a: Export trade is the sale of goods and services from one country to another, while import trade is the purchase of goods and services from a foreign country for use in the domestic market.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Export and Import Trade'.
questions.a: Export earns foreign exchange for the exporting country, while import supplies goods that are not produced domestically or are cheaper from abroad.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Export and Import Trade'.
questions.a: What is export trade?

concepts.title: Joint Venture and Wholly Owned Subsidiary

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Joint Venture and Wholly Owned Subsidiary' refers to.
questions.a: A joint venture is a business arrangement where two or more firms share ownership, control, and risk in a foreign market, while a wholly owned subsidiary is a company fully owned and controlled by a foreign parent firm.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Joint Venture and Wholly Owned Subsidiary'.
questions.a: Joint ventures share risk and resources with a local partner, while wholly owned subsidiaries give full control but require the highest investment and risk in a foreign market.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Joint Venture and Wholly Owned Subsidiary'.
questions.a: What is a joint venture in international business?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'EXIM Policy' refers to.
questions.a: EXIM policy, or export-import policy, is the set of rules and guidelines framed by a government to regulate and promote the country's foreign trade, covering exports, imports, tariffs, and incentives.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'EXIM Policy'.
questions.a: EXIM policy aims to promote exports, regulate imports, earn foreign exchange, and achieve a favourable balance of trade through incentives, duties, and trade agreements.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'EXIM Policy'.
questions.a: What is EXIM policy?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'World Trade Organisation (WTO)' refers to.
questions.a: The World Trade Organisation (WTO) is an international organisation established in 1995 that sets and enforces rules for international trade and aims to promote free and fair trade among member countries.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'World Trade Organisation (WTO)'.
questions.a: The WTO promotes free trade by reducing tariffs and barriers, settles trade disputes between members, and ensures that trade flows as freely, predictably, and fairly as possible.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'World Trade Organisation (WTO)'.
questions.a: What is the WTO?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Trade Blocks' refers to.
questions.a: Trade blocks are groups of countries that form an economic alliance to reduce or remove trade barriers such as tariffs and quotas among member countries while maintaining barriers against non-members.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Trade Blocks'.
questions.a: Trade blocks promote free trade among members through reduced tariffs and common policies, and examples include the European Union, NAFTA, ASEAN, and SAARC.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Trade Blocks'.
questions.a: What are trade blocks?

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'India's Foreign Trade' refers to.
questions.a: India's foreign trade refers to the export and import of goods and services between India and other countries, which has grown and diversified in composition since independence and economic liberalisation.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'India's Foreign Trade'.
questions.a: India's foreign trade has shifted from exporting primary products to exporting manufactured goods, software, and services, and plays a major role in the country's economic growth.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'India's Foreign Trade'.
questions.a: Explain the features of India's foreign trade.

questions.q: Explain in your own words what 'Documents for Export-Import' refers to.
questions.a: Export-import documents are the official papers required to move goods across national borders, including commercial documents like invoices and bills of lading and regulatory documents like licences and customs declarations.

questions.q: State the single key point to remember about 'Documents for Export-Import'.
questions.a: Export-import documents provide evidence of the transaction, transfer ownership, enable customs clearance, and secure payment, and errors can cause delays, penalties, or loss of payment.

questions.q: Give one standard exam phrasing that targets 'Documents for Export-Import'.
questions.a: What are export-import documents?
